# ADR-018: Keep liveness membership in its existing owner and cache source phase decisions

Status: chosen_for_partial_master_liveness

Concerns: Q-state, Q-behavior, Q-evidence

## Decision

Extend Tracking with separate keep-alive registration and group membership using source-bound typed rules. Cache dead free entities before control; skip source phases and temporarily project those entities to static rigid bodies for the existing Avian schedule. Re-read liveness for proximity and preserve the final check/clear.

## Rationale

Original InDeadBubble reads actual sets, including stale or phantom IDs, and exempts warp mode. Inferring membership from current balls or recomputing motion gating after callbacks changes the source behavior.

## Alternatives

Inferring membership from current ball flags; a second tracker or physics integrator; recomputing the source cached flag during later phases.

## Consequences

One authoritative membership owner is serialized in source_partition_v1; the entity-keyed frame cache is derived and cleared at tick finish. Real CPython/C++ methods independently check typed set semantics. Full collision history, reentrancy, pending-work snapshots, malformed host objects, all configurations and mandatory proofs remain open. Existing client collision proof-fixture constructors receive the explicit live input through AST adaptation; all four concrete tests run in the existing engine library against actual kernels. Whole Kani crate imports and old partition fixture APIs remain incomplete, separately from successful ordinary test execution.
